sources.title: P4 Advanced Financial Management September/December 2016 - Official Answers
sources.use: Project duration and a worked selling-price sensitivity margin.
sources.finding: Duration is calculated as the PV-weighted average time. Selling-price headroom is NPV divided by the discounted, post-tax revenue cash flows affected.
sources.formula: Duration = Σ(t × PV_t) / ΣPV_t; selling-price sensitivity = NPV / PV of affected post-tax revenue cash flows.

sources.title: AFM September/December 2019 - Official Sample Answers
sources.use: Second, very explicit AFM project-duration calculation.
sources.finding: The answer totals PV × time and divides by total positive PVs, producing 3.04 years.
sources.formula: Project duration = total (PV × time) / total PV.

sources.title: F9 June 2016 Examiner’s Report
sources.use: Black-and-white statement of the general sensitivity formula.
sources.finding: The denominator must be the present value of the project variable affected, after relevant tax effects.
sources.formula: Sensitivity % = 100 × NPV / PV of project variable.

sources.title: FM September/December 2023 Examiner’s Report
sources.use: Current ACCA convention for variable sensitivity and discount-rate sensitivity.
sources.finding: For the discount rate, IRR minus the original rate is the absolute headroom in percentage points. ACCA says percentage sensitivity divides that change by the original rate.
sources.formula: Variable sensitivity % = NPV / PV of affected post-tax variable × 100. Discount-rate sensitivity % = (IRR − original discount rate) / original discount rate × 100.

sources.title: AFM March/June 2019 - Official Sample Answers
sources.finding: The answer identifies an 11% project-specific risk-adjusted cost of capital based on a proxy company asset beta, then discounts the project cash flows at 11%.
sources.formula: Use the project-specific RADR as the discount rate applied to the project’s relevant cash flows.

sources.title: FM March/June 2018 - Official Sample Answers
sources.use: Joint-probability ENPV table and ACCA explanation of RADR derivation.
sources.finding: The official answer constructs joint probabilities and ENPV, and explains that a proxy beta can be ungeared and regeared to obtain a project-specific discount rate.
sources.formula: ENPV = Σ(probability × outcome NPV); RADR may be derived through CAPM using a proxy beta ungeared and regeared.

sources.title: F9 June 2015 - Official Answers
sources.finding: The answer calculates an expected input using probabilities, carries it through the project cash-flow table, and labels the result ENPV.
sources.formula: Expected input = Σ(probability × outcome); ENPV is the NPV based on probability-weighted expected inputs/outcomes.

sources.title: AFM September 2018 - Official Answers (Airone / Washi Co)
sources.use: Calculator #11 (fxhedge.ts) FIX ROUND 2, 2026-07-23 - per-unit currency option premium formula, cited by the GPT adjudication round and independently re-verified here by direct fetch.

sources.title: AFM March/June 2021 Examiner's Report (currency futures/options hedge question)
sources.use: Calculator #11 (fxhedge.ts) FIX ROUND 2, 2026-07-23 - full worked lock-in-rate calculation, cited by the GPT adjudication round ("MJ21") and independently re-verified here by direct fetch. Algebraically checked against the engine's own formula and found to be an EXACT match under a sign-convention transposition (see finding).
sources.finding: The report's own convention defines basis = opening futures price − spot rate (the OPPOSITE sign to this engine's basis0 = spot0 − futures0), and its lock-in formula is 'opening futures price − basis remaining'. Substituting the sign-flip shows this is algebraically IDENTICAL to this engine's lock_in_rate = futures0 + unexpired_basis - both routes compute exactly 0.2374 US$/MR1 on the worked figures. Also confirms premium-currency conversion (not proration) is the graded error class the examiner flags, matching GATE 18's scope.
sources.formula: Worked: current basis = 0.2378 − 0.2358 = 0.0020; basis remaining = 0.0020 × 1/5 = 0.0004; lock-in rate = 0.2378 − 0.0004 = 0.2374 US$/MR1.

syllabus_sources.note: TWO-COLUMN LAYOUT, and the right extraction flag is NOT the one the AFM guide (E6) needs. syllabus_sources.label: ETH-CODE
syllabus_sources.edition: IESBA Handbook 2025 Edition, as adopted by ACCA effective 1 January 2026
syllabus_sources.issuer: IESBA, adopted in full and unaltered by ACCA as Section A of the ACCA Code of Ethics and Conduct
syllabus_sources.title: ACCA Code of Ethics and Conduct - Section A: International Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants (including International Independence Standards), Volume 1
syllabus_sources.use: THE marking basis for SBL section A3 ethics outcomes (A3a-A3d), and the source of record for any drill that classifies an ethical threat. THREE passages page-verified 20/08/2026: (1) PDF p.39 - S120.6 A3, the FIVE and only five threat categories, verbatim: 'Self-interest threat - the threat that a financial or other interest will inappropriately influence a professional accountant's judgment or behavior'; 'Self-review threat - the threat that a professional accountant will not appropriately evaluate the results of a previous judgment made, or an activity performed by the accountant or by another individual within the accountant's firm or employing organization, on which the accountant will rely when forming a judgment as part of performing a current activity'; 'Advocacy threat - ... will promote a client's or employing organization's position to the point that the accountant's objectivity is compromised'; 'Familiarity threat - the threat that due to a long or close relationship with a client, or employing organization, a professional accountant will be too sympathetic to their interests or too accepting of their work'; 'Intimidation threat - the threat that a professional accountant will be deterred from acting objectively because of actual or perceived pressures, including attempts to exercise undue influence over the accountant.' (2) PDF p.57, printed p.52 - S210.4 A1, Part 2 (Professional Accountants in BUSINESS), examples of circumstances that might create a conflict of interest, including verbatim: 'Being responsible for selecting a vendor for the employing organization when an immediate family member of the accountant might benefit financially from the transaction.' S210.2 frames a conflict of interest as creating threats to OBJECTIVITY. This is IESBA's own worked shape for a procurement-conflict scenario. (3) PDF p.371, glossary (printed p.363 onward) - 'Close family: A parent, child or sibling who is not an immediate family member.' and 'Immediate family: A spouse (or equivalent) or dependent.'
syllabus_sources.finding: A BROTHER-IN-LAW IS NEITHER IMMEDIATE NOR CLOSE FAMILY under the Code's own glossary, so a rubric that rests a self-interest threat on a brother-in-law's financial interest is resting it on a relationship the Code does not enumerate. Where the connection is the relationship itself rather than a financial interest held by the accountant or their immediate/close family, FAMILIARITY is the fitting category. Also settled here: an ABSENT independent review is not a self-review threat - self-review requires the accountant to re-evaluate the results of their OWN (or their firm's/organization's) prior judgment and RELY on it in a current activity, so a control that never happened creates no self-review threat, it leaves an existing threat uncontrolled.
syllabus_sources.note: FETCHED, NOT STORED - same posture as every other ACCA PDF here; 'official_acca_pdfs/' is git-ignored (.gitignore line 71). ADOPTION CHAIN, and it matters for citation: ACCA's Code of Ethics and Conduct was RESTRUCTURED on 1 July 2025 into three documents (Guide; Section A: IESBA Code; Sections B and C: Supplementary Requirements and Guidance). ACCA states it adopts the IESBA Code 'in full, using the original American English language text and interpretation' and adopts revisions 'in their entirety and unaltered' - so the threat definitions and the glossary are the IESBA text verbatim, and citing IESBA paragraph numbers IS citing ACCA's Code. Volume 1 holds Parts 1-4B plus the Glossary; Volume 2 (https://www.accaglobal.com/content/dam/ACCA_Global/Members/Doc/rule/ethics/1-Jan-26/CEC-2025-IESBA-Handbook-Vol-2-15-Dec-2026.pdf) is NOT registered - nothing in the SBL A3 outcomes needs it. A 10-page ACCA GUIDANCE FACTSHEET (https://www.accaglobal.com/content/dam/ACCA_Global/Members/members-in-practice/members-in-practice/Code-of-Ethics-and-Conduct-1-Jan-2026.pdf, 183946 bytes) quotes all five threat definitions compactly on its p.8 and is a useful locator, but it states on its own p.1 that it 'has no regulatory status' and that the Rulebook takes precedence - so it is deliberately NOT registered and must never be cited as the marking basis. EXTRACTION: pdftotext 4.00 is present on these machines; '-raw' works and gives correct reading order. The PDF has NO printed-page/PDF-page offset table - printed p.52 is PDF p.57, printed p.363 is around PDF p.371, so always cite the PDF page alongside the printed one.
syllabus_sources.gap_this_closed: Registered 20/08/2026. Before this, 34 sources were registered and NOT ONE was an ethics code, on a qualification whose SBL section A examines ethical threats and safeguards directly (A3a-A3d). SBL-A4 was authored against the taxonomy from memory and misclassified two of its three threats. That is below the standard the AFM risk (S1-S7) and fx-hedge (S8/S9, T1/T2) families were held to, where every convention carries a page reference.

technical_articles.formula: Contracts = $30m/$0.5m x 2mths/3mths = 40; premium = 0.255% x 40 x $500,000 x 3/12 = $12,750; swap saving = (3%-1%) x 1/2 = 1% pa excluding fees, then each party nets a 0.5% bank fee off their share.

technical_articles.title: How to answer an interest rate risk management question (ACCA P4/AFM technical article)
technical_articles.note: Live HTML page, not a stable PDF - no byte-guard applies; verified by direct WebFetch 2026-07-24.
technical_articles.use: Calculator #12 (IR hedging) Step-0 - the fullest worked depositor-side FRA/futures/options example found (D27,000,000 deposit), incl. the full futures expected-close-price mechanic through to net result under BOTH a rate-rise and a rate-fall scenario.
technical_articles.finding: Depositor buys futures ("Buy futures now (go long in the futures market), as the hedge is against a fall in interest rates") and buys CALL options ("Buy call options as need to hedge against a fall in interest rates"; exercise if strike below expected futures price). Contracts = notional/contract-size x deposit-period/contract-period (90 contracts worked). Basis = (100 - spot rate) - futures price; unexpired basis diminishes linearly by elapsed/total contract life (2/6 x 1.02 = 0.34). Expected closing futures price = 100 - expected rate - unexpired basis (NOT the FX lock-in-rate formula 'opening futures + unexpired basis' - the two families' formulas are structurally different because IR futures price = 100-rate while FX futures price is a currency rate). Gain/loss on futures = (closing price - opening price) x contract-size x contract-period/12 x contracts, netted against the money-market actual return/cost to give a net result and effective annual rate - reconciles to the SAME effective rate (4.58%) under both a rate-rise and a rate-fall scenario, confirming the hedge locks a single effective rate as designed.
technical_articles.formula: Contracts = D27,000,000/D500,000 x 5/3 = 90; basis = (100-4.20)-94.78 = 1.02; unexpired basis (31 Jan) = 2/6 x 1.02 = 0.34; expected futures price (rate=5.3%) = 100-5.3-0.34 = 94.36; futures gain/loss = (0.9436-0.9478) x D500,000 x 3/12 x 90 = (47,250); net result (both scenarios) = 515,250, effective annual rate 515,250/27,000,000 x 12/5 = 4.58%.

technical_articles.note: Live HTML page, not a stable PDF - no byte-guard applies; verified by direct WebFetch 2026-07-24.
technical_articles.use: Calculator #12 (IR hedging) Step-0 - confirms the linear-diminishing-basis assumption used across T4/T5 is the general ACCA convention, not a one-off worked-example artefact, and flags it as a simplifying assumption ACCA itself calls out as not holding in practice (this is the standard scepticism-mark hook seen in the Northney/Sohbet examiner reports).
technical_articles.finding: "Basis is the difference between the futures and spot prices" and "basis is often assumed to diminish at a constant rate", explicitly flagged as a simplifying assumption that "may not hold true in practice" - the source of the basis-risk discussion/scepticism marks referenced in the Abertafol and Sohbet examiner reports (E1, E4).
technical_articles.formula: Basis = spot price - futures price = (100-4.20)-94.78 = 1.02; unexpired basis (31 Jan) = 2/6 x 1.02 = 0.34.

technical_articles.title: Determining interest rate forwards and their application to swap valuation (ACCA P4/AFM technical article, Nov 2011)
technical_articles.note: Live HTML page, not a stable PDF - no byte-guard applies; verified by direct WebFetch 2026-07-24. A byte-identical PDF companion (sa_nov2011_intrateswaps.pdf) was also fetched and cross-checked - same content.
technical_articles.use: Calculator #12 (IR hedging) Step-0 - the ONLY ACCA technical article on interest rate swaps beyond T4's comparative-advantage example. Uses a DIFFERENT presentation: deriving annual forward rates from a company's spot yield curve, then solving for the swap's fixed-equivalent rate by NPV-ing the net swap flows to zero.
technical_articles.finding: Bank offers to swap a company's variable-rate loan payments for a fixed rate: "the company pays a fixed rate of interest to the bank in exchange for receiving a variable rate of return from the bank based on the above yield rates less 50 basis points" (a bank margin/spread taken off the floating leg, not a flat fee as in T4). The fixed-equivalent rate R is solved by setting the NPV of (variable receipt - R) over the loan life to zero, discounting at the spot yield-curve rates. "In practice the receipts and payments of the swap would be netted off" - year-by-year net cash flow is receipt-or-payment depending on sign, not a single flat annual swap payment. AMBIGUITY: this NPV/forward-curve swap style and T4's comparative-advantage swap style are BOTH on ACCA's technical-articles page but structurally unrelated - neither the SD23/MJ25/SD24 examiner reports (Abertafol/Sohbet/Northney) feature a swap requirement at all, so there is no recent real-exam anchor confirming which style (or a third, simpler style) AFM currently examines.
technical_articles.formula: One-year forward rate = spot(2yr)^2 / spot(1yr) (e.g. 1.0460^2/1.0350 = 1.0571, i.e. 5.71%); swap fixed rate R solves Σ[(variable_t - R) x 100m] x discount_factor_t = 0 across the loan life.

technical_articles.title: Foreign currency risk and its management (ACCA F9 technical article)
technical_articles.note: Live HTML page, not a stable PDF - no byte-guard applies; verified by direct WebFetch 2026-07-24. Already used informally (cited in a code comment, not registered) as the source for fxhedge.ts's money-market-hedge mechanism and the netting texture in K4 - this registration formalises that prior citation and extends it to the exposure-classification content.
technical_articles.use: E-section narrative batch (pipeline #2) Step-0 - the ONLY located ACCA source (F9-tier; no dedicated P4/AFM technical article exists on this topic per a direct check of the AFM technical-articles index) defining the three exposure types for E2a and the six 'dealing with transaction risk' methods relevant to E2a's 'how these can be managed' scope and E2c's netting/matching.
technical_articles.finding: Defines all three exposure types verbatim: Transaction risk - "This arises when a company is importing or exporting. If the exchange rate moves between agreeing the contract in a foreign currency and paying or receiving the cash, the amount of home currency paid or received will alter." Translation risk - "This affects companies with foreign subsidiaries. If the subsidiary is in a country whose currency weakens, the subsidiary's assets will be less valuable in the consolidated accounts... Usually, this effect is of little real importance to the holding company because it does not affect its day-to-day cash flows." Economic risk - "The source of economic risk is the change in the competitive strength of imports and exports" (worked example: a weakening euro makes UK exports less price-competitive in the eurozone). Lists six 'dealing with transaction risk' methods (invoice in own currency, netting, matching, leading and lagging, forward contracts, money-market hedging) plus 'further methods' (futures, options). AMBIGUITY: the article does NOT use the words 'internal' or 'external' anywhere in this context - that internal/external classification is a common tutor-textbook (BPP/Kaplan) framing, not ACCA's own vocabulary; encoding it as if it were an ACCA-stated convention would be an invented-framework risk (COMPLETENESS_GATE/jurisdiction-lint doctrine).
technical_articles.formula: None (purely qualitative/definitional article) - netting worked example: JPY 1m owed to a Japanese supplier netted against JPY 1.1m owed BY a Japanese subsidiary leaves net exposure of JPY 0.1m only; matching worked example: US$2m receivable 1 Nov against US$1.9m payable 15 Nov, deposited in a USD account, leaves US$0.1m exposure.

fae_research_sources_note: FAE Advisory research sources (docs/research/FAE_ADVISORY_CROSSWALK.md and FAE_REUSE_APPENDIX.md), registered 2026-08-30. ALL PUBLIC, ALL FETCHED-NOT-STORED. DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE the four arrays fetch_acca_sources.ps1 iterates (sources + examiner_reports + syllabus_sources + question_sources): two of these four are live HTML pages, and that script asserts a %PDF magic number and THROWS on anything else, so registering them there would break the fetch for every ACCA source too. Same disposition, and the same reason, as unverified_citations_do_not_bake_in above. The two PDFs carry bytes + sha256 so a silent re-issue is detectable by hand. CAI IP discipline (see syllabus_sources E7) applies to all four: never committed, never indexed, never added to a vector store or RAG corpus. NOTE ON AUTHORITY, since these four are not equal: FAE-MARKING is CAI stating its own process and is authoritative; FAE-INFOSCHEME is CAI stating its own product terms and is authoritative; FAE-CASSI25 is a STUDENT SURVEY and is authoritative only for the indicator roster it reports; FAE-BARDEN23 is a 2023 examiner interview and is DESIGN evidence, not current marking authority.

fae_research_sources.label: CASSI-FAE25
fae_research_sources.title: CASSI FAE Education Report 2025 (post-exam student survey, 352 respondents)
fae_research_sources.issuer: Chartered Accountants Student Society of Ireland (CASSI), published on the CAI website
fae_research_sources.use: docs/research/FAE_ADVISORY_CROSSWALK.md. Section 6.3 'Advisory (ADV)' is the only located public document that names the ACTUAL indicators of a real FAE Advisory sitting (2025), indicator by indicator, across both simulations. 42 of the 352 respondents sat the ADV elective.
fae_research_sources.finding: The 2025 Advisory paper ran EIGHT indicators over two simulations. Simulation 1: Indicator 1 Cash Flow / Working Capital ('multiple asks (up to nine in some readings)'); Indicator 2 Foreign Exchange ('five separate asks'); Indicators 3 & 4 Macro Environment / Leadership ('The leadership change management question was clear and familiar (e.g., Kotter's model)'). Simulation 2: Indicators 5 & 6 Valuation and Acquisition ('The requirement to apply both P/E and DCF methods was seen as appropriate but demanding'); Indicator 7 Operating Leverage ('Many respondents had not encountered the concept during their studies'); Indicator 8 Performance Measurement ('generally regarded as clear and well aligned with the syllabus (e.g., Balanced Scorecard)'). Section 7.4 records that respondents 'strongly recommended that the Institute should provide a marking scheme for sample papers' - candidate-side corroboration of the crosswalk section 5 gap (indicator-level calibration is not published), which is distinct from the marking PROCESS, and that IS published (FAE-MARKING).
fae_research_sources.caveat: THIS IS A STUDENT SURVEY, NOT A CAI EXAMINER REPORT. Everything about difficulty, fairness, wording and syllabus coverage is respondent PERCEPTION and carries no marking authority. What it is good for is the INDICATOR ROSTER - a factual account of what the 2025 Advisory paper asked - and that roster is checkable against the crosswalk's competency labels. Do not cite its opinion content as CAI's position.
fae_research_sources.ip_restriction: FETCHED, NOT STORED. Public CAI-hosted PDF, but treated under the same CAI discipline as E7: not committed, not indexed, not added to any vector store or RAG corpus. No local copy is kept in the repo.

fae_research_sources.label: CAI-MARKING
fae_research_sources.title: Marking checks and processes (Chartered Accountants Ireland, Information and Appeals Scheme)
fae_research_sources.format: Live HTML page - NOT a PDF, so no byte-guard and no filename; see fae_research_sources_note.
fae_research_sources.use: docs/research/FAE_ADVISORY_CROSSWALK.md section 5. This is the page that OVERTURNS the first pass's claim that 'CAI does not publish how it marks'. It is the primary evidence behind correction 1 in crosswalk section 7.
fae_research_sources.finding: Four safeguards, verbatim: (1) 'a number of qualified, chartered accountants mark some sample scripts (all markers mark the same script) and discuss various approaches to marking and possible alternative answers'; (2) 'markers involved in marking the same question/case study, must "test mark" scripts and undergo a process of aligning their marking approach, so that they are all marking consistently'; (3) 'each marker is moderated by a "moderator" or senior marker, that is, the moderator will remark scripts which have been marked by the marker and will compare the outcomes. Any variances are followed up'; (4) 'at CAP2, all marginal scripts are independently double marked. Where small variances arise, the candidate is given the benefit of the higher mark... At FAE, all scripts are independently double marked and any variances discussed with the examiner or their assistant(s).'
fae_research_sources.caveat: It describes the marking PROCESS, not the marking STANDARD. Knowing every FAE script is double-marked says nothing about how far a point must be developed to score, which is the gap crosswalk section 5 actually names. Do not let 'CAI publishes its marking process' slide into 'CAI publishes its marking scheme' - the second is false, and buying the first-hand version of it is what FAE-INFOSCHEME is for.
fae_research_sources.ip_restriction: FETCHED, NOT STORED. Quoted here for evidence under the same CAI discipline as E7; the page itself is not committed, indexed or added to any retrieval corpus.

fae_research_sources.label: CAI-BARDEN-23
fae_research_sources.title: FAE Exam Guide 2023 - 'Your official guide to FAE preparation and success' (Chartered Accountants Ireland in association with Barden)
fae_research_sources.use: docs/research/FAE_ADVISORY_CROSSWALK.md section 4.4 - DESIGN evidence for how much work one indicator is expected to carry, which is the input to the indicator-detector and the equal-time-budget model.
fae_research_sources.finding: FAE Core Examiner Q&A, printed p.6: 'Yes, we are going to ask students to perform up to three or four pieces of work per Indicator and we will not apologise for that. So, structure is vital.' The same Q&A states that indicators are deliberately BLENDED across syllabus areas - 'We are actively blending the Indicators we develop for the FAE Core paper. It is more reflective of what happens in reality' and 'Indicators in this area tend to blend with other elements of the syllabus; we are actively starting to do this in exam questions' - direct evidence that compound/blended indicators are designed in, not incidental, which is what makes decomposition decisive under the equal-marks rule.
fae_research_sources.caveat: TWO SCOPE LIMITS, both load-bearing. (a) The quote is from the FAE CORE examiner Q&A, NOT the Advisory elective - it is evidence about how CAI's examining team designs indicators generally, and must not be reported as an Advisory-specific statement. (b) It is the 2023 edition: DESIGN EVIDENCE, NOT CURRENT MARKING AUTHORITY. Note also that the wording is 'up to three or four pieces of work per Indicator' - 'up to' is a ceiling, not a fixed count, and quoting it as 'three or four pieces per indicator' overstates it.
fae_research_sources.ip_restriction: FETCHED, NOT STORED. Publicly hosted by Barden; not committed, not indexed, not added to any retrieval corpus.

fae_research_sources.label: CAI-INFO-SCHEME
fae_research_sources.title: Information and appeals scheme (Chartered Accountants Ireland) - the Information Scheme
fae_research_sources.format: Live HTML page - NOT a PDF, so no byte-guard and no filename; see fae_research_sources_note.
fae_research_sources.use: THE HIGHEST-VALUE INDICATOR-LEVEL CALIBRATION ROUTE IDENTIFIED SO FAR for the gap named in crosswalk section 5 - the only located route to real CAI marks and real examiner comments on a real FAE script.
fae_research_sources.finding: Two products, both purchasable on the student portal. Option A: 'Candidates will be provided with their marks per paper, broken down into mark per question, per section'. Option B - tutorial report plus breakdown of marks: 'Candidates will be provided with comments for each question they answered and a summary of how they performed during their exam.' Availability, verbatim: 'The above reports can only be purchased through the student portal for seven days after the results are published and for the current session only.' Eligibility: offered 'to candidates who have received a result of "fail" in any of the papers which they sat' and 'not available to students who have received a "pass" in a paper which they sat'. It IS available for FAE: 'Information Scheme is not available for CAP1 exams as these are auto marked' and 'As of 2026, the Information Scheme is not available for CAP2 exams as these exams are auto marked' - FAE is excluded from neither. The script is not re-marked as part of the process.
fae_research_sources.time_bound: FAE Summer 2026 results are published 4 September 2026, so the seven-day purchase window CLOSES 11 SEPTEMBER 2026. The next window is the FAE Autumn 2026 session, results 29 January 2027. Both dates verified 2026-08-30 from CAI's own timetable page (https://www.charteredaccountants.ie/Current-Student/Exams/Timetables-Exams-Assessments): 'FAE Summer 2026 exam session ... Results published date: 4 September 2026'; 'FAE Autumn 2026 exam session ... Results published date: 29 January 2027'.
fae_research_sources.caveat: CORRECTION TO THE BRIEFING'S FRAMING - THE INFORMATION SCHEME DOES NOT YIELD THE SCRIPT. Verbatim: 'students are not provided with a copy of their script as part of the tutorial report. Students wishing to apply for a copy of their script need to submit an access request to the privacy manager.' So 'real script, real marks, real examiner comments' is TWO routes, not one: the Information Scheme buys the MARKS BREAKDOWN and the EXAMINER COMMENTS; the SCRIPT requires a separate subject-access request to CAI's privacy manager, which is not bounded by the seven days but is also not immediate. Three further limits, all structural: only a FAILING candidate is eligible, so the calibration sample can never include a strong script and is skewed to the bottom of the distribution; it is current-session only, so it cannot be reconstructed later; and the whole route depends on a trainee's consent and on their willingness to share a failed result. It is the best route identified, not a clean one.
fae_research_sources.ip_restriction: FETCHED, NOT STORED. Quoted for evidence under the same CAI discipline as E7; not committed, not indexed, not added to any retrieval corpus. Any material actually obtained under this scheme is a third party's personal exam data and requires that trainee's explicit, informed consent before it is read, quoted or used for calibration.
